0.0.n: 何 asks what the progress rate refers to.

0.1.n: の links the question word to 進捗率, asking what the rate measures.

0.2.n: 進捗率 is the proportion of a target already achieved.

0.3.n: This is part of でしょう, a polite question ending that invites consideration.

0.4.n: う completes でしょう; it is not a separate word here.

1.0.n: この comes directly before a noun to identify it.

1.1.n: Here, 進捗率 refers to progress toward the full-year profit target.

1.2.n: に marks what the speaker focuses attention on.

1.3.n: やっぱり is a conversational form of やはり, reinforcing the importance of this focus.

1.4.n: 注目する becomes 注目して, followed by いく to suggest continuing the examination.

1.5.n: と introduces what follows from examining the rate.

2.0.n: この points to the April–June period being discussed.

2.1.n: 4 shares 月 with 6 in 4〜6月, meaning April through June.

2.3.n: 6 combines with 月 to name the final month of the range.

2.4.n: 月 follows month numbers; here it applies to both ends of the range.

2.5.n: の links April–June to the description of it as a three-month period.

2.6.n: か月 counts months, and 間 emphasizes the duration.

2.7.n: で marks the time span within which the profit was achieved.

3.0.n: 年間 sets the yearly scope of the profit figure.

3.1.n: の connects 年間 to the following profit expression.

3.2.n: 通期 refers to the entire accounting period, rather than one quarter.

3.3.n: 利益 is the financial measure being compared with its full-year target.

3.4.n: に対して identifies the full-year profit as the basis for comparison.

4.0.n: 何 combines with パーセント to ask how much of the target was achieved.

4.1.n: ぐらい makes the requested percentage approximate rather than exact.

4.2.n: できました is the polite past form of できる, referring here to achieving part of the profit target.

4.3.n: か closes the question that the speaker then quotes.

4.4.n: って is a conversational alternative to と for quoting the preceding question.

4.5.n: いう works with って and の to package the quoted question as an idea.

4.6.n: の turns the preceding quoted question into something that can serve as the subject.

4.7.n: が marks the quoted idea as what the speaker identifies as 進捗率.

4.8.n: Here, the term is defined as the percentage of the annual profit target achieved.

4.9.n: な connects the noun 進捗率 to the explanatory ending んです.

4.10.n: ん is shortened の and signals that the speaker is explaining the term.

4.11.n: です makes the explanation polite.

4.12.n: けれども gently links this explanation to the next point, without necessarily expressing a strong contrast.

5.0.n: 単純 combines with に to describe how the speaker is presenting the calculation.

5.1.n: に lets 単純 describe the manner of explaining rather than a noun.

5.3.n: 四半期 is one three-month part of a fiscal year.

5.4.n: です politely states that the periods being discussed are quarters.

5.5.n: から follows the statement to give the reason for using 25% increments.

5.6.n: The percent unit is omitted but understood from the discussion.

5.8.n: Repeating 25 suggests adding an equal share each quarter.

5.9.n: 積み上げる becomes 積み上げて, followed by いく to show accumulation over time.

5.10.n: 感じ presents the calculation as a rough picture rather than a strict rule.

5.11.n: な connects 感じ to the reason-giving ending んで.

5.12.n: んで is conversational ので, giving a reason for the figures in the next line.

6.0.n: 第 makes a number indicate order; 第1 identifies the first quarter.

6.1.n: 四半期 combines with 第1 to name the first three months of the fiscal year.

6.2.n: は sets the first quarter as a topic, contrasting it with the halfway point.

6.3.n: The percent unit is understood even though it is not spoken here.

6.5.n: 中間期 refers to the first six months of the fiscal year in this financial context.

6.6.n: は introduces the first-half period as the second comparison topic.

6.7.n: 50 pairs with the following % sign to give the cumulative halfway target.

6.9.n: という introduces the preceding figures as the content of the conclusion.

6.10.n: こと packages the preceding statement into an idea within ということになります.

6.11.n: に marks the resulting conclusion with なります.

6.12.n: なります is the polite form of なる; here it presents the logical result of the calculation.

0.lit: Progress rate of what might it be?
0.tip: 何の asks what something relates to; でしょう makes the question polite and reflective.

1.lit: If we continue focusing, after all, on this progress rate,
1.tip: 注目する uses に to mark the thing receiving attention.

2.lit: Over this three-month period of April through June,
2.tip: In 4〜6月, the single 月 applies to both numbers.

3.lit: Relative to the annual full-year profit,
3.tip: に対して marks the reference figure against which progress is measured.

4.lit: The question of approximately what percentage was achieved is the progress rate, but,
4.tip: っていうの turns the quoted question into an idea the speaker can define.

5.lit: Simply, since these are quarters, it is like continuing to build up 25, 25, so,
5.tip: Repeating 25 suggests equal quarterly additions, with percent left understood.

6.lit: As for the first quarter, 25; as for the first half, 50%—that is what it works out to.
6.tip: ということになります presents these percentages as the logical conclusion of the preceding explanation.
